who: Aaron John Ihde, historian of chemistry at Wisconsin–Madison; PhD Wisconsin 1941.

evidence.says: ACS biography identifies Aaron John Ihde, his Wisconsin doctorate in 1941, and his formal appointment to Wisconsin's History of Science Department in 1957.
Alan Rocke's 'Aaron Ihde and His Students,' pp. 15–23, discusses Ihde's Wisconsin doctoral students, including Hamlin, Hochheiser and Meyer.
Authority identifies Aaron J. (Aaron John) Ihde and cites History of Acid-Base Theory and Chemistry and Modern Society.

notes: Full name, Wisconsin career, field and named students identify the same historian.

who: Jean M. O’Brien, historian of Native American and Indigenous history at Minnesota; PhD Chicago 1990.

evidence.says: Minnesota's faculty profile identifies Jean O'Brien in History, with a history PhD from Chicago in 1990 and specialties in Native American and Indigenous Studies.
The candidate authority identifies John Thomas O'Brien, author of From Bondage to Citizenship (1990), rather than Jean O'Brien.
Rochester's commencement program lists John Thomas O'Brien Jr. in History with the thesis From Bondage to Citizenship: The Richmond Black Community, 1865–1867.

notes: Candidate p-62043 is John Thomas O'Brien, a different historian with a different doctoral institution and dissertation.

Identifies the Reelfoot Lake author as Russell Harvey Caldwell.

who: Edward F. Keuchel, American economic historian at Florida State; PhD Cornell 1970.

evidence.says: Florida State's bulletin lists Edward F. Keuchel as professor of history, with service dates 1970–2001.
The 1975 foreword identifies editor Edward F. Keuchel of Florida State's History Department, with a Cornell PhD in American history and a specialty in American economic history.
The Edward F. Keuchel authority cites Civil War Marine (1975) and Florida, Enterprise under the Sun (1990).

notes: The authority's Civil War Marine is the same publication that identifies the Florida State professor and Cornell doctorate.

who: Morton Rothstein, economic and agricultural historian at Wisconsin and later UC Davis; PhD Cornell 1960.

evidence.says: Records his Cornell PhD in 1960, Wisconsin History Department service from 1962 to 1984, and subsequent UC Davis appointment and Agricultural History editorship.
Identifies Morton Rothstein as professor of history at UC Davis, editor of Agricultural History since 1984, and a scholar of agricultural trade.
The other candidate is associated with SUNY Buffalo's Division of Cell and Molecular Biology and Biochemical Approaches to Aging.

notes: n93000309 matches the Wisconsin-to-Davis historian; n82043197 identifies a different scholar in biology.

who: Johann Peter Sommerville, historian of early modern Britain and political thought at Wisconsin; PhD Cambridge 1981.

evidence.says: His CV gives the name Johann Peter Sommerville, Cambridge PhD 1981, and Wisconsin appointments from 1988 onward; lists Politics and Ideology in England and Thomas Hobbes.
The candidate is John Sommerville of the Department of Zoology, University of St Andrews, associated with Electron Microscopy (1987).

notes: John Sommerville the zoologist is different from Johann Peter Sommerville the Wisconsin historian.

who: Catherine Evtuhov, historian of imperial Russia at Columbia; PhD Berkeley 1991.

evidence.says: Columbia identifies Catherine Evtuhov as professor, with a 1991 Berkeley PhD in Russian and European history; lists The Cross & the Sickle and The Cultural Gradient.
The 2018 university profile describes her second year at Columbia after a Georgetown appointment following her Berkeley dissertation in 1991.
The Catherine Evtuhov authority cites The Cross and Sickle (1996) and The Cultural Gradient (2002).

notes: The candidate's LC identity and works match Columbia's professor; doctorate and appointment period agree with the supervisor record.

who: Linda Biesele Hall, historian of modern Mexico and Latin America at New Mexico; doctorate Columbia.

evidence.says: UNM identifies Linda Hall as a Columbia-trained historian, a UNM professor from 1986 until retirement in 2016, and author of Álvaro Obregón (1981) and Texas and the Mexican Revolution (1984).
Authority expands Linda B. Hall to Linda Biesele Hall and cites Álvaro Obregón (1981) and Texas and the Mexican Revolution (1984), including the usage Linda Hall.

notes: The exact works connect the candidate authority to UNM's professor; institution, teaching period and doctoral university agree.
